_comment: Ratchet floors for crates exempt from the §0b 90% bar (PM ruling 2026-09-06). The gate FAILS if a crate drops below its floor and RAISES the floor when a merge exceeds it, so an exemption can never be used to go backwards. Committed deliberately: a floor kept only in CI state is a floor nobody can review in a diff.

pending_crates.wheel-sqlite: SDK is extracting the journal logic into this crate so wheel-engine and wheel-host share ONE implementation — the host's store opens first on the deployed machine and still had the crash-looping version. New crate, so it meets the 90% bar from the start: no floor, no exemption. Recorded here only so its arrival is expected rather than a surprise, and so wheel-engine's count DROPPING by four reads as the storage_mode tests moving rather than as coverage lost.

_wheel_engine_floor_note: Raised 72.88 -> 80.34 from CI run 34083949556 on main 9ebdf05, which measured wheel-engine at 80.34% (10106/12579). The ratchet raises the floor automatically and prints COMMIT IT, but CI discards its working copy — so without this commit the next run measures against 72.88 and a 7.5-point gain from SDK's new code is silently given back. The floor is an exemption from the 90% bar, so it only ever moves UP: it exists to make an exemption impossible to use as a way to go backwards.
